description:
## Why
fz-nhb.11 makes the parser read Elixir's `(A, B -> R)` beside fz's own `(A, B) -> R`. Two spellings of one type is a concept added; this ticket removes the extra one.

## What changes
- Every `(..) -> ..` function type outside parentheses in lib/*.fz (116 spec/type lines on 248d23229), fixtures and guides is rewritten as `(.. -> ..)`.
- `parse_paren_or_arrow` refuses a `->` after the closing `)` with a spanned diagnostic naming the Elixir spelling.
- Decide with the owner: Elixir refuses a type variable used once or not declared in `when` (229 of 741 lib specs use one); refuse it as Elixir does, or keep it as an fz extension and document it.
  Fixture 01080's subject is such a variable (`@spec count([a]) :: integer when a: var`; Elixir: "type variable a is used only once"). Refuse: 01080 becomes a diagnostic fixture or states its subject another way, and its twin is deleted. Keep: 01080 keeps its twin and fz-nhb.19 lists it.

## Signal
No `) ->` function type remains in lib, fixtures or guides; the refusal has a fixture; full gate green.

## Collision
lib/*.fz is edited by other sessions (Optimize, fz-engine R2); sequence through the coordinator.
title: One function-type spelling: lib specs use Elixir's (A, B -> R) and fz's (A, B) -> R is retired
